title: Vitor Pereira agrees to take Nottingham Forest head coach job
author: Nick Miller
content:
Vitor Pereira has agreed to take the Nottingham Forest head coach job.

Forest dismissed Sean Dyche after less than four months in charge following a goalless draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers, who sit bottom of the table, on Wednesday.

The Athletic reported on Thursday that Forest had identified former Wolves boss Pereira as a strong candidate to replace him and they were progressing in talks. Pereira was appointed by Wolves in December 2024, sparking an upturn in results that saved them from relegation that season. He was sacked, however, in November after failing to win any of their first 10 league games of the term and has been out of work since.

Dyche was the third coach to be dismissed by Forest this season, after the earlier sackings of Nuno Espirito Santo and Ange Postecoglou, and had been under contract until 2027.

Forest chose the 54-year-old as a replacement for Postecoglou in October, with the side in 18th, after making contact with former Manchester City and Italy manager Roberto Mancini and considering an approach for Fulham’s Marco Silva.

Dyche did not manage to move Forest clear of safety and they sit three points above the relegation zone having won only three of their last thirteen games in all competitions.

Forest are next in action against Fenerbahce in the first leg of their Europa League play-off tie on Thursday.

Analysis by Paul Taylor

Vitor Pereira was the man Nottingham Forest targeted as the replacement for Sean Dyche when they decided to make a change in the dugout on Wednesday night.

Forest hope the Portuguese can repeat the early success he had at Wolverhampton Wanderers, when he led them out of the bottom three in the Premier League to a mid-table finish, following his appointment in December 2024.

By the following April, Wolves were 12 points clear of the relegation places.

He takes over a Forest side who sit three points clear of 18th-placed West Ham — and who are looking to find some stability, amid a chaotic campaign that sees Pereira arrive as the fourth manager.

Pereira’s first task will be to take Forest to face one of his former clubs, Fenerbahce, in the Europa League play-off round in Turkey next Thursday.

But his priority will be to ensure that a dramatic campaign does not end with a return to the Championship, for a club that fought for 23 years to win promotion back into the top flight, via the play-offs in 2022.
